title: Mumbai Indians Part Ways With Coach Mahela Jayawardene After Ninth-Place Finish
excerpt: The five-time champions and their three-title coach agreed to split in search of a 'fresh perspective', with interviews for a successor expected in the coming week.
body:
• Mumbai Indians and head coach Mahela Jayawardene have mutually parted ways, the franchise announced on October 17, saying it wants a "fresh perspective" for the next IPL cycle.
  • Jayawardene, 49, won three IPL titles with MI (2017, 2019, 2020) across two stints as head coach, but the five-time champions finished ninth in IPL 2026 with only four wins.
  • MI have shortlisted candidates for the job and expect to interview in the coming week; Jayawardene is unlikely to stay on in another role.
  • He is the third high-profile coaching exit of the year, after Stephen Fleming's departure from Chennai Super Kings.

Mumbai Indians have ended one of the IPL's most successful coaching partnerships. The franchise and Mahela Jayawardene mutually agreed to part ways on Friday, closing the Sri Lankan's second stint as head coach as MI look for what they called a fresh perspective ahead of the IPL 2027 cycle, The Times of India reported.

The decision was finalised at a meeting of the franchise's top brass earlier this week. MI have already identified several candidates and expect to hold interviews in the coming week, with an announcement to follow. Jayawardene is unlikely to remain in the set-up in a different capacity, according to reports — a clean break rather than a reshuffle.

A record few coaches can match

Jayawardene first took charge in 2017 and immediately delivered a title, adding championships in 2019 and 2020 — the latter making MI the first side to defend an IPL crown in nearly a decade. He stepped into a group role as global head of performance in 2022, overseeing the wider MI family across leagues, before returning as head coach in October 2024 on a two-plus-one contract.

https://x.com/mipaltan/status/2111359294683611550

The second stint never reached those heights. MI reached the playoffs in 2025, losing in Qualifier 2, then collapsed to ninth in 2026 with just four wins in a season marked by injuries, availability problems and reported dressing-room unrest, Sports Now reported.

"Mumbai Indians has been a very special part of my journey for over a decade now. I leave with immense pride in what we have achieved together and will always carry a special place in my heart for MI."

— Mahela Jayawardene

Farewells from the top

Team owner Nita Ambani thanked Jayawardene for a contribution that went beyond results. "His calm leadership, integrity and deep love for the game have meant so much to us," she said in the franchise statement carried by Latestly. "Mahela will always be a part of our #OneFamily."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=hL_8NlthvGo

The exit continues a season of churn at the top of the IPL. Jayawardene is the third head coach to leave a franchise this year, after Stephen Fleming's departure from Chennai Super Kings, and Delhi Capitals have also changed coaches. For MI — the league's joint-most successful franchise, watched by a large diaspora audience across the US, Gulf and Australia — the next appointment sets the direction for the whole 2027 cycle, from retentions to auction strategy.

What happens next

Interviews are expected within days and MI want the new coach in place well before retention decisions lock. Whoever takes over inherits a squad with a championship core, a restless fan base, and a simple brief: a ninth-place finish cannot repeat.
